finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test forwards attacker-controlled req.body.callback directly to axios.post with no URL validation, allowing server-side requests to internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints. Redirects are followed by default, so no first-hop check helps.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:19-20), entry on the unauthenticated pub router (routes.js:4, 19)
finding.sink: axios.post(req.body.callback, { ping: true }) at routes.js:20; status returned at routes.js:21

trace.note: pub is a plain express.Router() with no auth middleware
requireAdmin is attached only to the admin router, not pub
POST /hooks/test handler on pub, reads req.body.callback

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, IP-range, port, or allowlist validation; no redirect restriction (axios follows redirects by default); no auth on pub route in this file. Auth status depends on mounting code (app.js), which is not in the repo, so unauthenticated exposure is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-20 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post with no scheme, host, IP, or allowlist check, and axios follows redirects by default. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, 12) is attached only to the admin router, not pub (routes.js:4).
verdict.reason: All trace lines match the file (routes.js:4, 12, 19, 20, 21), and req.body.callback at routes.js:20 is set by whoever sends the request with no closing guard, so any caller who can reach the pub router can make the server request internal or metadata hosts. Whether that caller is unauthenticated depends on how app.js mounts pub, which is not in the repo, so the "unauthenticated" framing is unverified, though the SSRF holds for any non-admin caller that can reach the route.

finding.claim: Admin-gated GET /diagnostics/fetch forwards attacker-controlled req.query.url directly to axios.get with no URL validation. Same root cause as SSRF-1; exploitable only by an admin session, so lower severity.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:14-15), entry on the admin router
finding.sink: axios.get(req.query.url) at routes.js:15; status returned at routes.js:16

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applied to all admin routes, enforced via return

finding.guards_checked: Admin role check is enforced (return used, applied before the route on the same router). No URL validation, no host/IP-range allowlist, no redirect restriction.

verdict.guard_found: routes.js:7-9 requireAdmin returns 403 unless req.session.role === "admin", applied to every admin route at routes.js:12 via admin.use. This is an authorization gate, not URL validation, so it does not validate the URL. It does restrict the source to admin sessions.
verdict.reason: The trace misdescribes routes.js:12, which is admin.use(requireAdmin) and enforces the check by not calling next(), not "via return". The source is not attacker-controllable by a low-privilege remote attacker because routes.js:12 and routes.js:8 restrict /diagnostics/fetch to admin sessions, so the only party who can set req.query.url is already an admin, and the finding's own "lower severity" framing concedes this. The candidate's claim that it is exploitable only by an admin session therefore does not meet the confirmation criterion.
